repositories.citation: [1] Martian. 'Model Router - Dynamic LLM Routing Platform.' withmartian.com, 2025. https://withmartian.com/
key_features: Patent-pending LLM router with model mapping technology
Automatic model selection via collective intelligence approach
Claimed 75% success rate vs 35% Claude Haiku, 55% Claude Sonnet
Cost reduction up to 99.7% by eliminating wasteful premium model use
LLM Judge: custom annotation for model performance
Model Gateway: unified access to hundreds of LLMs
repositories.architecture: Model mapping approach - creates simplified representations of AI systems to predict performance without running models. Uses collective intelligence by routing queries to models with specialized strengths. Claims to achieve 20% improvement over GPT-4o, Claude Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro.

routing_approach.learning_mechanism: Router adjusts based on user behavior and metrics

code_quality.integration_effort: minimal - single line of code change

repositories.usage_example: Import package, add API key, modify one line where LLM calls occur. Router automatically directs prompts to optimal models.
limitations: Enterprise focus may limit startup accessibility
repositories.competitive_position: Market leader with strongest enterprise traction and strategic Accenture partnership. First mover with patent-pending technology.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: HIGH - Direct competitor with automatic model selection and cost optimization. More mature with enterprise customers.

repositories.citation: [2] Not Diamond. 'AI Model Router with Custom Training.' notdiamond.ai, 2025. https://www.notdiamond.ai/
key_features: Custom router training from evaluation data
Beats all foundation models on major benchmarks
repositories.architecture: Meta-model approach - builds single interface between application and inference layers. Trains custom routers using evaluation data to predict which model will provide highest quality response for any input. Emphasizes network of specialized models over monolithic model approach.

routing_approach.learning_mechanism: Custom router training on user's specific data
routing_approach.model_selection_basis: Predicted quality per input based on training

repositories.usage_example: Out-of-the-box router for immediate use, or train custom router with evaluation data for specific use cases.
repositories.customer_results: Samwell AI: 10% improvement in output quality with 10% reduction in inference costs and latency
limitations: Requires evaluation data for custom training
repositories.competitive_position: Strong technical team with impressive angel investors from Google, OpenAI, GitHub, Adobe. Focus on customizable routing with training.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: VERY HIGH - Custom training approach aligns with learning from usage. Fast routing (60ms) and quality focus matches SkillRunner goals.

repositories.citation: [3] Lenton, Daniel. 'Unify - Router for LLM Selection.' Unify AI, 2024. https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/chime-ai

stats.team_size: 7 employees at funding, planned to add 3
stats.users: ~3,000 signups, few hundred regular users (as of May 2024)

key_features: Router tool with parameter-based model selection
Joint optimization for quality, cost, and speed
Supports new model providers within 1-2 days of release
repositories.architecture: Neural network router that learns which models are best for specific tasks. Uses objective benchmarks to compare models across providers. Provides dashboards for comparison.

routing_approach.model_selection_basis: Joint optimization of quality, cost, speed

limitations: Smaller user base compared to competitors
UK-based may limit US enterprise adoption
Limited public documentation on technical approach
repositories.competitive_position: YC-backed with strong European presence. Only competitor claiming joint optimization of quality, cost, and speed. Academic roots from Imperial College.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: HIGH - YC connection valuable. Neural network approach for learning model-task fit aligns with SkillRunner's goals.

repositories.citation: [4] LMSYS. 'RouteLLM - Open-Source Framework for Cost-Effective LLM Routing.' GitHub/LMSYS, 2024. https://routellm.dev/
key_features: Routes between strong model (GPT-4o) and weak model (GPT-4o mini)
Multiple routing methods: SW Ranking, Matrix Factorization, BERT-based, Causal LLM
Analyzes complexity, length, task type in milliseconds
repositories.architecture: Framework providing multiple routing algorithms. Matrix factorization model learns scoring function. BERT classifier and causal LLM classifier predict which model provides better response. Analyzes query complexity dynamically.

routing_approach.type: Multiple approaches: ML-based (matrix factorization, BERT, causal LLM) and threshold-based
routing_approach.complexity_detection: Analyzes complexity, length, task type in milliseconds
routing_approach.learning_mechanism: Learns from preference data and human evaluations
routing_approach.model_selection_basis: Predicted response quality based on query characteristics

repositories.usage_example: Uses preference data to train router. Dynamically routes queries between strong and weak models based on complexity analysis.
repositories.performance: Cost reduction over 85% on MT Bench, 45% on MMLU, 35% on GSM8K compared to GPT-4 only
limitations: Limited to binary routing (strong vs weak model)
repositories.competitive_position: Academic gold standard. Open source provides transparency. Strong research backing from LMSYS (creators of Chatbot Arena).
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: MEDIUM - Open source framework valuable as reference implementation. Binary routing is simpler than SkillRunner's multi-model approach.

key_features: Large model catalog with sortable pricing and availability
Automatic router to pick best option
Prepayment credits, volume discounts, annual commits
repositories.architecture: Managed LLM gateway with unified API. Provides routing shortcuts for optimization goals (speed vs cost). Acts as abstraction layer over 100+ model providers with OpenAI-compatible interface.
repositories.usage_example: Use OpenAI SDK, change endpoint to OpenRouter, add API key. Use model shortcuts like :nitro or :floor for automatic optimization.
repositories.pricing: Pay per token consumed, no markup over provider pricing. No monthly fees. Transparent pricing per million tokens.
limitations: Free tier too limited for production use
repositories.competitive_position: Market leader for managed gateway with broad adoption. Strong for developers wanting unified API but limited intelligence in routing.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: LOW-MEDIUM - Provides infrastructure (gateway) but lacks intelligent routing. No automatic task complexity detection or learning.

repositories.citation: [6] BerriAI. 'LiteLLM - Open Source LLM Proxy and Router.' GitHub, 2025. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm
key_features: Python SDK and Proxy Server (AI Gateway)
Cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, logging
Multiple routing strategies: simple-shuffle, least-busy, usage-based, latency-based
Auto routing based on input content
Per-project, API key, and model budgets and rate limits
repositories.architecture: Self-hosted proxy server with flexible routing engine. Router tracks deployments independently, manages health and cooldown. Provides unified interface across providers with automatic failover.

routing_approach.complexity_detection: Auto routing rules based on input content
routing_approach.model_selection_basis: Configurable: weighted pick, load balancing, latency, usage

repositories.usage_example: Self-host proxy, configure routing strategies in config file, define auto-routing rules for specialized models based on content.
limitations: Requires manual configuration of routing logic
repositories.competitive_position: Leading open-source alternative to managed gateways. Strong for teams wanting control and customization.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: MEDIUM - Open source reference. Has routing infrastructure but lacks intelligent complexity detection and learning from usage.

repositories.citation: [7] Keywords AI. 'LLM Developer Platform with Routing.' Keywords AI (YC), 2024. https://www.keywordsai.co/

repositories.architecture: Developer platform with basic keyword-based routing. Analyzes query characteristics to determine routing between cost-effective and premium models.
limitations: Keyword detection prone to false positives/negatives
Limited to binary routing (cheap vs expensive)
repositories.competitive_position: Early stage YC startup. Basic approach suggests opportunity for more sophisticated solutions.
repositories.proximity_to_skillrunner: LOW - YC connection valuable but approach is too simplistic. Shows demand for better routing solutions.

Focus on gateway features rather than smart routing

repositories.architecture: High-performance proxy with observability focus. Thin layer adding minimal latency while providing monitoring, caching, and failover. Emphasis on cost tracking and optimization.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Startup building automatic routing from scratch
implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Start with RouteLLM framework as reference, implement ML-based routing with matrix factorization
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Open-source provides proven approach. ML-based learns from usage. Can differentiate from rule-based competitors while avoiding patent issues with Martian's model mapping.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Need fast time-to-market with basic routing
implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Use LiteLLM or OpenRouter as infrastructure, build intelligence layer on top
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Leverage existing gateway infrastructure. Focus differentiation on intelligent routing algorithm rather than rebuilding gateway. Faster to market.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Enterprise customers requiring security and compliance
implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Study Credal AI's approach - multi-factor routing with policy enforcement
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Enterprise buyers prioritize security and compliance. Need routing that considers data sensitivity, not just cost/performance.

implementation_recommendations.scenario: Optimizing for cost with quality constraints
implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Implement threshold-based routing like RouteLLM with learned thresholds
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Binary routing (strong/weak model) achieves 85%+ cost reduction. Add learning to optimize threshold per task type.

implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Start with keyword/heuristic rules, collect usage data, transition to ML
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Need data to train ML models. Bootstrap with rules, then use real usage to train better models over time.

implementation_recommendations.recommended_solution: Focus on custom training per customer (Not Diamond approach) and reinforcement learning from outcomes
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Most competitors use generic routing. Customer-specific training and learning from actual outcomes (not just predicted quality) provides clear differentiation.

competitive_positioning_for_skillrunner.positioning_statement: SkillRunner: The open-core intelligent LLM router that learns from your actual results. Unlike rule-based gateways (OpenRouter, LiteLLM) or black-box enterprise routers (Martian), SkillRunner provides transparent, explainable routing that adapts to your specific workload through reinforcement learning from real outcomes. Start with open-source routing, upgrade to custom-trained intelligence for your use case.
target_segments: AI-native startups building agent systems (vs enterprise for Martian/Credal)
Developer teams wanting control and transparency (vs managed black box)
Companies with specific use cases needing custom routing (vs generic routers)
Cost-conscious teams needing 50%+ savings without quality loss
